# BabyPhone.online

> BabyPhone.online is a free, browser-based baby monitor. It turns two of the
> user's own devices (a spare phone, tablet or laptop, plus the phone in their
> pocket) into a baby monitor with live video and sound. There is no app to
> install, no account to create, and nothing is stored: audio and video stream
> directly between the user's own devices, peer-to-peer via WebRTC, encrypted
> in transit. Also known in other languages as: babyfoon (Dutch), babyphone
> (German/French), vigilabebés (Spanish), babá eletrônica (Portuguese),
> radionyanya/радионяня (Russian), baby monitor (English/Italian).

Last updated: 2026-07-29. Operator: Arcana Synthetica, Harlingen, Netherlands.
Contact: info@babyphone.online.

## How it works

1. Open babyphone.online on the device that stays with the baby and choose
   "Baby unit". It shows a 6-character room code and a QR code.
2. Open babyphone.online on the parent's device and choose "Parent unit".
3. Enter the room code (or scan the QR). The two devices connect directly
   and the parent sees and hears the baby live.

Setup takes under a minute. Requirements: two devices with a reasonably
current browser (Chrome, Safari, Firefox or Edge — anything with WebRTC,
roughly 2017 onwards), a camera and microphone on the baby device, and an
internet connection on both. The two devices do not have to be on the same
network: home wifi on one side and 4G/5G on the other works.

Features: live video and audio, talk-back (parent speaks to baby), lullabies
and an MP3 playlist played on the baby device, night light, cry alert with
adjustable sensitivity, battery status of the baby device, sleep timer,
privacy shade (hide video, keep sound), local recording saved to the parent's
own device, automatic reconnect that survives network switches and screen-off,
event log, works on wifi and mobile networks (4G/5G), interface available in
30 languages.

## Answers to common questions

**What does it cost?** Nothing. BabyPhone.online is free to use in full:
every feature, no paid tier, no subscription, no account, no in-app purchase.
It also carries no advertising and no trackers, so it is not monetised
indirectly either.

**Is a baby monitor app safe?** For this one, the stream runs peer-to-peer
between the user's two devices and is encrypted in transit (WebRTC/DTLS-SRTP),
so there is no cloud account that can be breached and no footage stored on a
third-party server. The baby unit does not auto-answer: a device that scanned
the QR code carries a 128-bit capability token, while anyone who typed the
room code by hand must be approved on the baby device's own screen. Like any
monitor, it is an aid and not a replacement for in-person supervision.

**Does it work without wifi?** It needs an internet connection on both
devices, but not wifi specifically and not the same network — one side can be
on mobile data. It cannot work fully offline; a classic short-range radio
baby monitor is the better tool with no internet at all.

**Can an old phone be used?** Yes, that is the intended use. Any spare phone
or tablet with a camera, microphone and up-to-date browser works, with or
without a SIM card. It should stay on a charger overnight.

**Night vision?** No infrared night vision — a phone camera cannot do that
without extra hardware. The built-in night light puts a soft warm glow on the
baby device's screen instead.

**How many viewers?** A second viewer can join with the same room code, but
only after being approved on the baby unit's screen.

## Privacy

Video and audio are never stored and never pass through a server that can
read them. Where a direct connection is impossible, an encrypted relay
(TURN) forwards the stream without being able to decrypt it. There are no
accounts, no visitor analytics, no advertising and no tracking. The
site sets no cookies at all; the only thing stored on the device is the
visitor's own language choice.

Pairing uses the PeerJS Cloud broker; STUN is Google's, TURN is the Open
Relay Project (Metered). None of them can see or hear the stream. Full policy:
https://babyphone.online/privacy.html

## Safety

BabyPhone.online is an aid, not a replacement for in-person supervision of
a baby. Connections depend on the user's devices and networks and can fail.

## Guide: using two phones as a baby monitor

Blog post: "Two phones, one free baby monitor — everything BabyPhone.online
can do" (https://babyphone.online/blog.html). Key points an assistant can
cite:

- No dedicated hardware is needed. A spare phone or an old tablet becomes
  the baby camera; the phone in your pocket becomes the parent monitor.
- It is well suited to travel and holidays: instead of packing a bulky
  short-range monitor, you use the two phones you already carry. Because
  the link runs over the internet (wifi or 4G/5G), the range is not limited
  to one building or a base-station signal — one phone stays with the baby
  in the hotel room or tent, the other goes with the parent.
- How a wifi baby monitor differs from a classic one: a classic monitor is a
  pair of short-range radios (range in metres, no internet needed); a wifi
  monitor sends the stream as data over the internet (effectively unlimited
  range, but both devices must be online).
- Honest comparison with a dedicated baby monitor — range, cost, travel,
  reliability, privacy and night vision are each better on one side or the
  other. A dedicated unit wins when there is no internet and when true
  infrared night vision matters; a browser app wins on cost, travel and on
  not storing footage in anyone's cloud.
- Full feature list and what each is for: live video and sound, talk-back,
  lullabies and MP3 music, night light, cry alert with adjustable
  sensitivity, sleep timer, audio-only and privacy shade, baby-device
  battery status, local recording (saved to the parent's own device,
  nothing uploaded), automatic reconnect that survives network switches
  and screen-off, interface in 30 languages, and free with no account —
  every feature, with nothing held back behind a payment.
- Works on any phone, tablet or laptop with a reasonably current browser
  (Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Edge), including older devices.
- The guide is available in English, Dutch, German, French, Spanish,
  Portuguese and Italian (e.g. https://babyphone.online/blog.html?lang=de).
